Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:10:1.hebrew: וצריכא - לאשמעינן בכולהו, דמי שאסר עצמו בדיבורו נאסר, ומי שלא אסר עצמו אינו נאסר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:10:1.english: And it is necessary - To teach us in all of them that whoever forbade himself by his statement is forbidden, and whoever did not forbid himself is not forbidden.

Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:10:2.hebrew: גבי דידיה - כי אמר קידשתיך, לא מיתסרא איהי בקרוביו, משום דאיהו שקורי משקר, וגברא לא איכפת ליה אם אוסר עצמו בקרובותיה חנם:
Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:10:2.english: With regard to himself - When he says, "I betrothed you," she is not forbidden to his relatives, because he is lying, and a man does not care if he forbids himself to her relatives for nothing.

Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:10:3.hebrew: ומקרי ואמר - קדשתיה, ואע"ג דלא קדשה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:10:3.english: And he happens to say - “I betrothed her,” even though he did not betroth her.

Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:11:1.hebrew: אבל איהי - כי אמרה "קדשתני", דאסרה נפשה אכולי עלמא עד שיתן לה גט, אי לאו דקים לה דקדיש לא הוה אמרה; ונתסר איהו על פיה בקרובותיה, ואפי' לא נתן לה גט:
Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:11:1.english: But [as for] her - When she says, “You betrothed me,” since she forbids herself to the entire world until he gives her a bill of divorce, if it were not certain to her that he betrothed [her], she would not have said [it]; and let him be forbidden to her relatives upon her word, even if he did not give her a bill of divorce.

Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:12:1.hebrew: מדרבנן הימנוה - רבנן לאמה על הבת, ותהא צריכה גט, ותאסר בקרובותיו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:12:1.english: By rabbinic law they deemed her credible - [The] Rabbis [deemed] the mother [credible] regarding the daughter, and [the daughter] would require a bill of divorce and be forbidden to his relatives.

Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:14:1.english: [The court] forces - [Him] to give her a bill of divorce.

Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:14:2.hebrew: לא כופין איכא כו' - דאין צריכה ממנו גט, דהא קתני: ״מותרת בקרוביו״; ואי בעיא גט, הוה מיתסרא באחיו, דהויא לה גרושת אחיו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:14:2.english: [Whether] we do not compel is [applicable], etc. - For she does not need a bill of divorce from him, as it teaches: “She is permitted to his relatives”; and if she required a bill of divorce, she would be forbidden to his brother, as she would be his brother’s divorcee.

Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:14:3.english: And rather, to the latter clause - Where she says, “You betrothed me,” so that she requires a bill of divorce:

Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:15:1.english: Granted, they request - Of him to give a bill of divorce:

Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:15:2.hebrew: לחיי - שצריך בקשה לאסור עצמו בקרובותיה, כדי להתירה לינשא, הואיל ואין חפץ בה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:15:2.english: [It is] well - That a request is needed [asking him] to forbid himself to her relatives in order to permit her to marry, since he has no desire for her.

Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:15:3.hebrew: ומקרי ואמר - קדשתיה, ואע"ג דלא קדשה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:15:3.english: And he happens to say - “I betrothed her,” even though he did not betroth her.

Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:16:1.hebrew: ושמעתתא דרב ושמואל אהדדי אתמר - לא לחלוק זו על זו באו, אלא להוסיף האחרון מה שלא פירש הראשון:
Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:16:1.english: And the teachings of Rav and Shmuel were stated together - They did not come to disagree with one another, but rather for the latter to add what the first did not explain:

Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:17:1.hebrew: ואם נתן מעצמו - בלא בקשה, כופין אותו ליתן כתובה, דגלי דעתיה דקדשה, וארוסה יש לה כתובה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:17:1.english: And if he gave of his own accord - Without [being asked by] a request, [the court] compels him to give [her] a marriage contract, for he revealed his mindset that he betrothed her, and a betrothed woman is entitled to a marriage contract.

Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:18:1.english: Both of them concede - To the words of the witness.

Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:18:2.hebrew: מהו - הא דתניא "אין חוששין" — משום דלא מהימן הוא, והא הימנוה? או דלמא, משום דאין קדושין חלין בלא עדים, ויליף "דבר" "דבר" מממון: כתיב בעריות "ערות דבר" (דברים כד), ובממון כתיב "על פי שני עדים יקום דבר" (שם יט):
Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:18:2.english: What is [the law]? - Is that which is taught [in the baraita], "one need not be concerned," because he is not believed — and [here] behold, they believe him? Or perhaps [is it] because betrothal does not take effect without witnesses, and it derives [this via a verbal analogy of] "matter" [from] "matter" from monetary law: regarding illicit relationships it is written, "a matter of unchastity" (Deuteronomy 24), and regarding monetary law it is written, "by the mouth of two witnesses shall a matter be established" (ibid. 19)?

Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:18:3.hebrew: אין ולא - לא היה מחזיק בדבריו, לא לאיסור ולא להיתר: פעמים שאמר הן, ופעמים שאמר לאו. ורפיא בידיה — ולא היתה מוחזקת הוראה זו בידו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:18:3.english: Yes and no - He did not hold firmly to his words, neither to forbid nor to permit: at times he said "yes," and at times he said "no." "And it was uncertain in his hand" — and this ruling was not firmly established in his hand.

Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:18:4.english: It was also stated - We do not read "also".

Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:19:1.hebrew: ואי ליכא עדים - ואפי' מודה, אמאי אסור בקרובותיה ע"פ עצמו? הלא אינן קידושין אפילו לדבריו! דאי נמי אמר "בעד אחד הוו קידושין בששניהם מודים", היכא דאין עד אחד לא אמרת; דעד אחד חשיב לחייב שבועה בדיני ממונות, הלכך בערוה נמי חשיב להתקיים קידושין בפניו, ובלבד שיהו שניהם מודים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:19:1.english: And if there are no witnesses - And even though he admits [having betrothed her], why is he forbidden to her relatives based on his own admission? Behold, it is not a [valid] betrothal even according to his [own] words! For even if one were to say, "With one witness it is a [valid] betrothal when both of them admit," where there is not [even] one witness you would not say [so]; for one witness is of significance to obligate an oath in monetary law, therefore in [matters of] forbidden relations as well he is of significance for betrothal to take effect in his presence, provided that both of them admit [to it].

Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:19:2.hebrew: אלא לאו בעד אחד - וקתני: "הוא אסור בקרובותיה", אלמא זה שמודה לו נאסר, דחשיב לאיתפוסי קדושין קמיה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:19:2.english: Rather, is it not with one witness - And it teaches: "He is forbidden to her relatives." Thus, this [party] who agrees with him is forbidden, for [a single witness] is considered [significant enough] for betrothal to take effect before him.

Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:1:1.hebrew: אמצעית שבכת שניה תשתרי - ארישא קאי, דמספקא לכל כת שניה בגדולה. אמצעית — לגבי מאן קרי לה גדולה, אי לא לגבי קטנה דההיא כת? אלמא, בכת אחת פליגי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:1:1.english: The middle [daughter] of the second group should be permitted - [The question] refers to the first clause [of the Mishnah], which leaves the entire second group in doubt regarding [the designation] "the elder [daughter]." As for the middle [daughter], relative to whom could he call her "the elder [daughter]," if not relative to the younger [daughter] of that [same] group? Evidently, they dispute [even] with regard to a single group.

Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:1:2.hebrew: בשאין שם - בכת שניה שום אמצעית. להכי תני: ״אסורות כולן״, אבל אי הוי התם אמצעית — הוי תני מתניתין: ״חוץ מן הקטנות שבקטנות״, ולא הוה תני: ״חוץ מן הקטנה״:
Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:1:2.english: Where there is not there - In the second group, any middle [daughter]. That is why it taught: "All of them are forbidden." But had there been a middle [daughter] there, the Mishnah would have taught: "Except for the younger [daughters] of the younger [group]," and it would not have taught: "Except for the youngest [daughter]."

Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:20:1.hebrew: קידשתיה בפני פלוני ופלוני - דהוו להו קידושין גמורין לכל דבריו, ונאמן הוא לאסור את עצמו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:20:1.english: I betrothed her in the presence of so-and-so and so-and-so - For according to his [own] words, it was a complete betrothal, and he is believed to forbid himself.

Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:21:1.hebrew: ולנה עמו בפונדקי - ואפי' לאחר זמן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:21:1.english: And she lodged with him in an inn - And even after [some] time.

Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:21:2.english: If there are witnesses - That she was betrothed through intercourse.

Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:21:3.english: Rather, is it not with one witness - And both of them admit [to it].

Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:22:1.hebrew: וליטעמיך - דאמרת, דאי ס"ל דאסורות אאמצעית נמי קאי — הוה מפרש לה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:22:1.english: And according to your reasoning - In that you say that if [the Tanna] held that [the ruling] "they are forbidden" applies to the middle [daughter] as well, he would have specified [her].

Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:23:1.hebrew: לא כופין איכא כו' - דאין צריכה ממנו גט, דהא קתני: ״מותרת בקרוביו״; ואי בעיא גט, הוה מיתסרא באחיו, דהויא לה גרושת אחיו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:23:1.english: [The ruling of] “we do not force” applies, etc. - For she does not require a bill of divorce from him, as [the mishna] teaches: “She is permitted to his relatives”; and if she required a bill of divorce, she would be forbidden to his brother, as she would be his brother’s divorcee.

Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:23:2.hebrew: ואלא אסיפא - דאמרה קדשתני, דבעיא גט:
Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:23:2.english: And rather, [it refers] to the latter clause - Where she said, "You betrothed me," such that she requires a bill of divorce.

Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:2:1.english: And so too, it is reasonable - That we are dealing with [a case where] there is no middle [daughter].

Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:2:2.hebrew: דאם איתא דאיכא - אמצעית, וכולהו בעי לאשמועינן דאסירן — נתנייה גבי "אינו יודע", ונימא הכי: "ואינו יודע אם גדולה שבגדולות, אם גדולה שבקטנות, או אמצעית שבקטנות — כולן אסורות". אלא מדלא תנייה לאשמעינן בה איסורא, שמע מינה סבירא ליה דלא אסירא; וכי קתני "כולן אסורות" — בדליכא אמצעית:
Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:2:2.english: For if it is so that there is - a middle [daughter], and [the Tanna] wants to inform us that all of them are forbidden, let him teach [it] in [the clause of] "and I do not know," and let him say this: "And I do not know if [it was] the eldest of the older [group], if the eldest of the younger [group], or the middle [daughter] of the younger [group] — all of them are forbidden." Rather, since he did not teach it to inform us of a prohibition regarding her, learn from it that he holds that she is not forbidden; and when he teaches "all of them are forbidden," [it is] in [a case] where there is no middle [daughter].

Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:2:3.hebrew: וליטעמיך - דאמרת, דאי ס"ל דאסורות אאמצעית נמי קאי — הוה מפרש לה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:2:3.english: And according to your reasoning - For you said that if he held that "they are forbidden" applies to the middle [daughter] as well, he would have specified her.

Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:2:4.hebrew: אמצעית שבכת ראשונה - דודאי אסירא אם ישנה שם, דהא מודים דכל כת ראשונה לגבי כת שניה גדולה קרי לה ואסורה — ניתנייה ברישא, כי היכי דנשמע מינה דאסורות עלה קאי, ולא תיסק אדעתין למישרי ולומר דכי קתני כולן אסורות — כשאין שם אמצעית:
Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:2:4.english: The middle one of the first group - For she is definitely forbidden if she is there, as [all] agree that any [daughter of the] first group relative to the second group is called "elder" and is forbidden — let [the Mishnah] teach her in the opening clause, so that we may learn from it that "are forbidden" refers to her, and it would not enter our minds to permit [her] and to say that when it teaches "all of them are forbidden," [it is only] when there is no middle daughter there.

Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:3:1.hebrew: הכי השתא - בההיא לא איצטריך ליה לפרושי. דאף ע"ג דמתניתין כולה בשאין שם אלא שתים בכל כת, לא תיסק אדעתין דאי הוה שם אמצעית לא הוה תני כולן אסורות — דכיון דתנא קטנה דידיה לאיסורא, ואשמעינן דקרי לה גדולה, כ"ש אמצעית דקשישא מינה. אלא כת שניה — דכי לא תנא לה, איכא למימר דמתניתין בשאין שם אלא גדולה וקטנה, אבל אמצעית לא הוה קרי לה גדולה — אם איתא דאיכא אמצעית ואכולהו קאי אסורות, ליתנייה בהדיא ונשמע דאף היא אסורה, דלא נטעי לאוקמא בשאין שם אמצעית:
Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:3:1.english: How can [these cases] be compared? - In that [case of the first group], it was not necessary for [the Tanna] to specify [her]. For even though the entire Mishnah [deals with a case] where there are only two [daughters] in each group, it would not enter our mind that had there been a middle [daughter] there, he would not have taught "all of them are forbidden"; for since he taught the younger [daughter] of its [group] for a prohibition, and informed us that [the father] calls her "the elder," all the more so the middle [daughter], who is older than she [is forbidden]. But [with regard to] the second group, where, when he did not teach her, it can be said that the Mishnah [is dealing with a case] where there is only an elder and a younger [daughter], but a middle [daughter] he would not have called "the elder" — if it is so that there is a middle [daughter] and "forbidden" refers to all of them, let him teach her explicitly, and let us learn that she too is forbidden, so that we would not mistakenly establish [the Mishnah as referring to a case] where there is no middle [daughter].

Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:5:1.hebrew: והרי פסח וכו' ופליגי - דאיכא למ"ד, לימים אמצעיים נמי קרי "פני", הואיל ויש מאוחר ממנו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:5:1.english: And behold, Passover, etc., and they disagree - For there is one who holds that one also calls the intermediate days "the front" [penei], since there is [a day] later than it.

Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:6:1.hebrew: התם בלישנא דעלמא פליגי - דמאן דאסר, לאו משום דסבירא ליה דכל שיש מאוחר ממנו קרי פני, אלא משום דמשמע ליה בלשון בני אדם: מיפני פיסחא קאמר — שיהא הפסח פנוי, פונה ועובר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:6:1.english: There they disagree with regard to the general usage of language - For the one who forbids [him until Passover ends, it is] not because he holds that whatever has [a time] later than it is called penei ["before"], but rather because it implies to him that in the language of people, he was saying "until Passover clears away" — that Passover should be cleared out, turning [away] and passing.

Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:7:1.english: He is forbidden to her relatives - For he has rendered them upon himself [like] a piece of forbidden [matter] through his admission.

Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:8:1.hebrew: ומותר בקרובות קטנה וכו' - שאין אמה נאמנת עליה, ואף היא אינה צריכה גט; דאי בעיא גט — הויא לה גרושתו, ונאסר בקרובותיה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 65a:8:1.english: And he is permitted to the relatives of the younger [woman], etc. - For her mother is not believed concerning her, and she does not even require a bill of divorce; for if she required a bill of divorce, she would become his divorcee, and he would be forbidden to her relatives.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 65a:16:1.hebrew: ואם נתן גט מעצמו כופין אותו ליתן כתובה - מכאן יש להוכיח, דאלמנה מן האירוסין יש לה כתובה, ואפילו לא כתב; דהא מסתמא הכא מיירי דלא כתב לה, דאי כתב לה — א"כ מאי "מבקשין" שייך למימר הכא? אלא ש"מ דמיירי הכא דלא כתב לה כתובה, ואפ"ה קאמר: "כופין אותו ליתן כתובה". ובפרק הכותב (כתובות פט:), דבעי: "אלמנה מן האירוסין יש לה כתובה או אין לה כתובה?" — היה יכול להוכיח מהכא, אבל לא רצה; שהרי לא רצה להוכיח מהאמוראין, כי אם מן המשנה:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 65a:16:1.english: "And if he gave a bill of divorce of his own accord, they compel him to give a marriage contract" - From here it can be proven that a widow from betrothal is entitled to a marriage contract, even if he did not write [one for her]. For presumably here [the Gemara] is dealing with [a case where] he did not write [one] for her, because if he did write [one] for her, if so, how does [the phrase] "we request" apply to be said here? Rather, conclude from it that here it is dealing with [a case where] he did not write a marriage contract for her, and even so it states: "they compel him to give a marriage contract." And in the chapter [entitled] HaKoteiv (Ketubot 89b), where [the Gemara] raises the dilemma: "Does a widow from betrothal have a marriage contract or does she not have a marriage contract?", it could have proven [it] from here, but it did not wish to, for it did not wish to bring proof from the Amora'im, but only from the Mishnah.
